section: 18. European Pursuit: The Path of the Simulacrum
description: The five of them agreed in the tavern on a plan to traverse Europe to find and destroy the simulacrum. By midnight, the crowd in the tavern gradually dispersed.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "And how do we find a reasonable excuse to go take a look at that mansion."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Order three plates of oysters

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: @player13

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Size him up "An old soldier" #Wave to him "Come sit, friend"

conversation.speaker: player13
conversation.text: "Then I won't stand on ceremony." Leaving his seat, he sits at the table with the others.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Order a plate of oysters for this veteran

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Hearing my native language in a foreign land

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "We're tourists here" #Knock on the table "But as you know, things are a bit unsafe these days"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Look him up and down

conversation.speaker: player13
conversation.text: "Served in the Great War." Waving a finger in the air. "They even gave me a medal."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Must have killed a lot of Krauts, then."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "That's impressive."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #Look at him with slight curiosity

conversation.speaker: player13
conversation.text: "Just traveling." Wipes his wrist. "Just lost my job."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Ah, the postwar years are tough for everyone."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Interested in finding a new one? For some extra cash."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Similar to your old line of work."

conversation.speaker: player13
conversation.text: "Well, alright then. I don't have any plans anyway." Tilts his head. "And what you were talking about just now sounded quite interesting."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Perfect. As you can see, we're all Americans, and we're short on a local here in Europe."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Shocked by the teammate's rapid disclosure of information, but quickly recovers

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "The information we just found says the statue should have fallen into the hands of a leper in the 13th century. He came to France. His name was Fernandic."

conversation.speaker: player13
conversation.text: Close eyes and quietly organize and ponder this information.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #player2 stares dumbfounded at player4's actions, quickly scans the surroundings for anyone who looks like they might be Middle Eastern/Turkish.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "So, are you interested in joining us? Our client has provided us with a handsome reward."

conversation.speaker: player13
conversation.text: "Hmm... hearing you say that, the whereabouts of this statue are indeed shrouded in mystery... Good! I'm very interested."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Yeah, what's even more bizarre is that this statue is actually a suit of armor."

conversation.speaker: player13
conversation.text: "That's... getting a bit far-fetched, isn't it?" Laughs awkwardly.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "I think so too. I somewhat suspect that's just a bard's fantasy."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Bailan had just smoothed the wrinkles of his coat and stood up when his fingertips grasped empty air! His briefcase was gone. At the same moment, Madeleine suddenly slammed her soup spoon into the copper pot. "Damn it! Who knocked over my pickled cucumber jar at the back door?!" Everyone turned to see a figure wrapped in a military coat darting down the steps, the leather corner of a case flashing under the gaslight.

conversation.speaker: player13
conversation.text: "But... whether it's true or false, you have to see it with your own eyes!" Saying this, he suddenly stands up and dashes out of the tavern in one swift stride.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Something darted out"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Fall down, the oysters in hand, rush out the door

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The four of them chased until their lungs ached, the suitcase scraping and bouncing on the cobblestones with a piercing sound that allowed them to track it. Suddenly, the fleeing tramp ahead kicked a stray cat blocking the way with his boot and darted into the bridge arch over a tributary of the Somme.

conversation.speaker: player13
conversation.text: Follow into the bridge arch

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: As you crawl into the bridge arch, you find the pickpocket holding a switchblade to a tramp's throat, hissing: Hurry up and pick the lock, you idiot!

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: "What?" #Just woke up from a cardboard bed and was pulled up by a stranger, "Wait wait, put the knife down, let me take a look first!"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Before the pickpocket could speak, the four of them stood before Johnson

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: I haven't even finished my nap!

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Ask player2

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #Closely follow behind the team

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: "Sir, you're scaring me, I can't concentrate"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "What's this thief saying?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Wait, isn't this the bag snatcher?"

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: "This is delicate work..."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #Stealthily place a hand inside the coat, take out own pistol.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Pat Lun'er "Time to work"

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: "You see, my hands are still shaking..."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The pickpocket sprang up like a startled stray dog. He grabbed Johnson by the collar and dragged him back. "Everyone back off! Or I'll slit this tramp's throat!"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: What a mess

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Tsk, ..." #Even without understanding, realized the current situation.

conversation.speaker: player13
conversation.text: "Don't act rashly..." Yawns "That thing, isn't he trying to pick the lock? Just let him do it."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Isn't holding him like that making it harder to pick the lock?"

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: "I haven't even brought my toolbox over, how can I pick it?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Look at him with disdain "Why do you think we care about this tramp?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Indeed, nothing but paper."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "At least not as valuable as this" #Flick him a few coins "Are you willing to gamble your future freedom?"

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Belief arises from desire, if it is what you hope for, it will be answered, <player2>'s persuasion wish:

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "We don't need to be enemies, right friend"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Fuck... deal!" The pickpocket kicked Johnson away and lunged for the coins! "Three coins! Enough for two doses of morphine!" After getting the coins, he flung the suitcase like a sack towards Bailan's feet, then ran off splashing through the mud.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Dear sir, want to teach him a lesson?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "He'll get himself killed."

conversation.speaker: player13
conversation.text: "Excellent, looks like you handled him. Well done indeed."

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: "You motherfucker, think you can mess with me and run?!" #Shouts, pulling a spear from a nearby sack and throwing it.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "That's right."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Scum like that will be found dead in a ditch in a couple of months."

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: .ra roll

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Belief arises from desire; if it is what you hope for, it will receive a response. <player12>'s roll for Wish:

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Stop him.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #The suitcase has been through a lot; there's already plenty of mud on it, adding a bit more to its story.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Looks him up and down. "Sorry you were frightened because of us. As an apology, would you mind joining us for a simple meal? My treat."

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: #Goes over angrily to retrieve the spear. "No need, no need. That lunatic... sigh, my skills are rusty."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The spear tip grazed the pickpocket's buttocks and embedded itself in a wooden crate, scaring him so much he fell flat on the ground with a thud. He then scrambled up cursing, his swearing mixed with the sound of fleeing footsteps quickly swallowed by the wind of the Seine.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "You haven't had lunch, it seems."

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: "Oh, you speak English too! Thank goodness. I don't have many friends here." #It's clear these people have American accents, but finding someone to communicate with makes his eyes light up.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Then it's like meeting an old friend in a foreign land."

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: #His stomach indeed growls, and he laughs awkwardly. "True, these people are shady. They take advantage of my language barrier and often only pay me with a single meal for lunch."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Alright, we should get back to lunch. If we don't head back soon, old Henry will scold us."

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: "It's fine, I'm not hurt."

conversation.speaker: player13
conversation.text: "We only finished half of that meal earlier."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "That's right, let's go."

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: "That sounds wonderful! What are we eating?" #Swallows saliva.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Oysters."

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: "That works, better than the 'Stargazy Pie' back home."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Bread and red wine, a freshly opened Burgundy."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Gives a bow.

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: "Tsk tsk, living the good life. You all must be tourists here, right?" #Returns a proper British gentleman's bow to player4 as well, though he doesn't have a hat.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "We're Americans, so, yes."

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: "I'm player12, British. I've been stranded here for almost a year due to travel troubles."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "A year???"

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: "Actually, I'm kind of a tourist too."

conversation.speaker: player13
conversation.text: "Really? I'm also British, how should I put it... I joined halfway."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Rubs forehead, then pats player4's shoulder "Remember to learn a foreign language."

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: "Because there was a war going on recently, the roads were chaotic with soldiers and bandits. I got robbed and barely made it here alive."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Then you're really lucky to be alive."

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: "My passport and documents are all lost. I plan to get a fake one and continue my travel plans."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Hmm, do you want to come with us?"

conversation.speaker: player13
conversation.text: "Not planning to go back home and sort things out? Seems you're a determined person." Expresses respect for this person inwardly.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "We happen to be here on business and will eventually return to London."

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: "If I'm lucky, people give me some money; worse case, I can only get a meal. Because my actions are competing with the local locksmith industry, they drive prices down really hard..."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "We will pass through England."

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: "Ha, looking so disheveled, I'm embarrassed to go back, and there's no one at home anyway."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #Considers whether the Orient Express checks documents.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Well, we can help you with that, but it will require a bit of labor from you."

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: "Hmm... really?" #Also raises glass.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Don't judge a person by what they say, but by what they do." #Gestures to the oysters in front of him.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: According to the League of Nations passport system, post-WWI Europe gradually established modern border inspection systems. However, in practice: first-class passengers usually only need to show passports for registration when boarding; second and third-class may be spot-checked when crossing borders; and the frequency of border officials boarding for inspections depends on the international situation—during the tense Franco-German relations in the Rhineland in 1923, checks were stricter.

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: "Oh! Sorry for talking so much I forgot to eat!" #Grabs food and devours it ravenously, juices splattering.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Take it easy, don't choke. So, what do you say, deal?"

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: "Ah~ that's better" #After eating and drinking his fill, "Well... my passport money is about this much." #Quotes a not insignificant amount, blinking and watching their reaction.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Not a fake passport, we'll get it for you at the town hall."

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: "I can give you the passport when getting off the train or ship, I won't run away. I'm ultimately heading to Constantinople, it's quite a long journey."

conversation.speaker: player13
conversation.text: "That's really extravagant. I guess we don't have to worry about investigation funds on this trip?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "I don't have much money myself, but I have a wealthy boss."

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: "Really? You can get it for me? But I lost my ID, hard to prove..."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "It's fine, money makes the mare go."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #The green university student is shocked.

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: "I asked about the process, go here to get a stamp, then go there... such a hassle. They just told me: 'Go back and wait for notification!'"

conversation.speaker: player13
conversation.text: "Have you tried the British Embassy? If you explain the situation, they should be able to issue a temporary identity document."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Glances at him "If you don't give them a single penny, of course they'll tell you to wait for notification."

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: "With the war, the embassy is busy with this and that, my application was probably shelved."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Should I tell everything?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Of course you can recruit a companion, it's always good."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Repeat what was told to the veteran

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Subtly indicate negation

conversation.speaker: player13
conversation.text: "I don't know, maybe it's best to tell everything? At least there won't be other questions during the rest of the journey."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Finally indicate agreement

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: "Oh, that's not a big or difficult matter then, count me in. I can travel around various countries by train and complete my journey."

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Prayer received! Continuing to record the horror of the Orient Express for you. Currently 5082 texts recorded, time elapsed 25 hours 15 minutes 27 seconds.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: So, as the story last time said,
